subject: biochemistry
title: Protein folding, molecular chaperones, amyloidosis and prion conformational disorders

steps.tx: Polypeptide folding into native tertiary conformation is guided by the **thermodynamic** minimization of free energy. Hydrophobic amino acid side chains collapse into the protein interior away from water, while hydrophilic residues orient towards the aqueous surface. Molecular chaperones, including heat shock protein 70 and heat shock protein 60 chaperonins, bind exposed hydrophobic patches to prevent aberrant aggregation during synthesis.
steps.say: Protein folding minimizes Gibbs free energy by burying hydrophobic residues inside and exposing hydrophilic groups to water. Chaperones such as heat shock protein 70 and heat shock protein 60 bind exposed hydrophobic patches to prevent abnormal aggregation during translation.

steps.tx: Pathological **amyloidosis** develops when soluble globular proteins undergo conformational transition into insoluble cross-beta sheet fibrillar aggregates. These amyloid fibrils deposit in extracellular tissues, resisting normal proteolytic degradation and producing organ enlargement and functional failure. Under polarized light microscopy, Congo red-stained amyloid deposits exhibit diagnostic apple-green birefringence.
steps.say: Amyloidosis occurs when soluble proteins transition into insoluble cross-beta sheet fibrillar polymers. These fibrils resist proteolysis, depositing in extracellular spaces and causing organ failure. Under polarized light, Congo red-stained amyloid reveals diagnostic apple-green birefringence.

left.title: Systemic amyloid types
points: AL amyloid: monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains
AA amyloid: serum amyloid A in chronic inflammation
ATTR amyloid: transthyretin in familial or senile cardiac

right.title: Organ manifestations
points: Heart: restrictive cardiomyopathy and low voltage ECG
Nerves: peripheral sensory and autonomic neuropathy

steps.tx: Prion diseases represent transmissible **conformational** neurodegenerations mediated by infectious proteinaceous particles lacking nucleic acids. The normal cellular prion protein, rich in alpha-helices, undergoes spontaneous or template-driven refolding into the disease-causing scrapie prion isoform rich in beta-sheets. The abnormal conformer catalyses further conversion of normal proteins, causing rapid neurodegeneration and classic spongiform encephalopathy.
steps.say: Prion disorders are transmissible neurodegenerations caused by misfolded protein conformers. The normal alpha-helical prion protein refolds into the beta-sheet rich scrapie form. This abnormal isoform templates further refolding, causing rapid neuronal death and spongiform change.

steps.tx: Endoplasmic reticulum quality control eliminates misfolded proteins via **ERAD**, the endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation pathway. Chaperones detect misfolded glycoproteins, retrotranslocate them across the membrane into the cytosol, and attach polyubiquitin chains. Cytosolic 26S proteasomes then degrade the ubiquitinated substrate. Severe ER stress activates the unfolded protein response, inducing apoptosis if homeostasis cannot be restored.
steps.say: Endoplasmic reticulum quality control identifies misfolded polypeptides and routes them through ERAD. Proteins are retrotranslocated to cytosol, polyubiquitinated, and degraded by 26S proteasomes. Unresolved ER stress triggers the unfolded protein response, initiating apoptosis.
